message.content:
A common example of a multi‑nucleated cell is **osteoclast**—a giant bone‑resorbing cell formed from the fusion of several monocytes/macrophages. Other well‑known multinucleate cells include:

| Cell Type | Typical Function |
|-----------|------------------|
| Osteoclast | Resorb bone tissue during remodeling |
| Skeletal Muscle Fiber | Contractile unit of voluntary muscles |
| Syncytial Cells (e.g., placenta villi) | Facilitate nutrient exchange between mother and fetus |

These cells contain more than one nucleus within a single cytoplasmic membrane, allowing them to perform specialized tasks efficiently.
